items.text: REFERRED TO CORPORATIONS, AUTHORITIES AND COMMISSIONS

items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the not-for-profit corporation law and the estates, powers and trusts law, in relation to reformation of charitable corporations and trust governance; and to repeal certain provisions of the not-for-profit corporation law and the estates, powers and trusts law relating thereto
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S7913

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend the not-for-profit corporation law
and the estates, powers and trusts law, in relation to reformation of
charitable corporations and trust governance; and to repeal certain
provisions of the not-for-profit corporation law and the estates,
powers and trusts law relating thereto

 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :

To improve and make clarifying amendments to the Nonprofit
Revitalization Act of 2013.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :

Section 1 - of the bill amends the definition of "independent
director" to:

*clarify that such definition applies to "key" non-employees of the
corporation;
*provide a different formula (using a sliding scale) to define
"independent";
*provide a definition for the terms "compensation" and "payment".

This section also provides exceptions to the definition of "real party
transaction" and a more comprehensive definition of "key person".

Section 2 - amends § 309 (Personal jurisdiction) of the NPCL to make
conforming amendments relating to the term "key person".

Section 3 - amends § 712 (Executive committees and other committees)
of the NPCL to clarify the power of the board to create committees,
and to limit the authority of such committees.

Section 4 - amends § 712-a (Audit committee) of the NPCL to repeal the
provision requiring the board or the audit committee to oversee the
implementation of conflict of interest and whistleblower policies.
(See, §§ 7 and 9 of bill, below.)

Section 5 - provides that an employee may serve as chair of the board
upon 2/3 vote of the entire board.

Section 6 - amends § 715 (Related party transactions) of the NPCL to
allow an authorized committee to determine whether a related party
transaction is fair, reasonable and in the best interest of the
corporation, and to provide a statutory defense in any legal action
involving a related party transaction.

Sections 7 and 9 - clarify that the board shall be responsible for
overseeing the implementation of the conflict of interest and
whistleblower policies.

Sections 8 and 10 amends § 715-a (Conflict of interest) and § 715-b
(Whistleblower) of the NPCL to clarify that conflict of interest and
whistleblower complaints shall be disclosed to the board or a
committee consisting of a majority of independent directors.

Sections 11 to 17 - make the above amendments to the parallel sections
in the EPTL.

Section 18 - sets forth the severability clause.

Section 19 - provides that the act shall take effect immediately.

 JUSTIFICATION :

In 2013, the Not-for-Profit Corporation Law underwent its first major
overhaul since its initial enactment in 1969, resulting in the
Nonprofit Revitalization Act of 2013.

Since its passage, recommendations have been made to improve the 2013
Act. The provisions of this bill correct certain inconsistencies, and
will make the statute operate more smoothly and efficiently.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

New bill

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

None to taxpayers.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
Immediately
